turns.text: The previous story examined GoogLeNet / Inception. Now the camera turns to ResNet and a new question along the same timeline: Why did researchers need ResNet, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?
ResNet introduced residual connections that let very deep networks learn refinements instead of full transformations. It made hundreds of layers trainable and became a backbone for vision systems.
A shortcut path adds the input back to a learned residual transformation.

Experts generally treat ResNet as a turning point in very deep network design. Its long-term legacy is residual learning: the shortcut-connection pattern that made depth easier to optimize and became a standard backbone idea across vision and beyond.
The thread continues with DenseNet, where researchers push the problem one step further.
